mappings.note: Which incident she could not believe (the principal's disciplinary action) -- a narrated event. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no appraisal of intent or style is asked.
Who influenced her personality most (the father) -- the text says so. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks who, not how she assesses him.

Mannu Bhandari is essentially a kahanikar -- placing the author in literary history. The frame has no biography or literary-history LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because her genre standing is not this lesson's content.
Why the father grew irascible (financial ruin) -- the stated cause. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: recall, not a reaction to his authoritarianism.

What it means that the house's walls spread across the whole mohalla -- the passage itself explains the idea, and the companion item on what 'ghar' meant carries the same content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the answer restates a fact rather than appraising the image.
Who Sheela Agrawal was -- a character introduced in the lesson. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: she is inside the text, not part of the author's bibliography.
Why the family moved to Ajmer -- the text's stated cause. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a life event, not a mantavya question.
How the suspicious streak passed from the father -- drawn from the narrated account. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content, not craft. (Stem says 'lekhak' where the text has a lekhika.)
What the father wanted for her -- stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: his stated wish, not a reaction to it.
What the principal requested of her father -- a narrated exchange. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
How far the mother had studied (not at all) -- the lesson states it. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: the mother is a figure in the text, so this is comprehension and not author biography.
Why the father left Indore for Ajmer (economic) -- the policy names Ajmer/Indore as LO-1 content. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
The elder sister's name (Sushila) -- a character in the text. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: a family member in the narrative, not bibliography.
How many siblings she had -- stated in the lesson. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: the text supplies the number, so it is comprehension.
Where Sushila went after her marriage -- a text fact about a character. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: this is the sister, not the author's own biography.

Authorship of 'Shekhar: Ek Jeevani' (Agyeya) -- literary history about another writer. The frame has no literary-history LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because the attribution is not this lesson's content.
Authorship of 'Tyag Patra' (Jainendra) -- literary history. The frame has no literary-history LO, which is why the competency is the honest citation and C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected.

Whom the writer married (Rajendra) -- author biography from the lekhak-parichay. The frame has no biography LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because this is not the prose text's vishayvastu.

Which magazine her husband edited (Hans) -- author biography. The frame has no biography LO, so the competency is the honest citation; C-H1.3-LO-1 was rejected because the fact sits outside the lesson. (Stem prints 'patrakar' where 'patrika' is meant.)

Gloss of 'aakrant', a word from the lesson -- a word's meaning in context, which the policy puts at LO-1. Rejected C-H1.2: a bare shabdarth is not one of the vyakaran categories this book routes to C-H1.2.
The mother's temperament (forbearing) -- description recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: no reaction to her silence is solicited.
Why the father was suspicious (betrayal by his own) -- the stated cause. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: recall of the text's explanation.

WHAT Mannu Bhandari said about her mother -- reproduce the text's account. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the companion item asking WHY she called her personality-less takes LO-2; this one asks only what she said.
The lekhika's opinion on tradition and the older generation's hold -- explicitly her raay, i.e. mantavya. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: no narrated fact answers it.
The reasons she gives for the father's late suspiciousness -- stated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the causes are narrated, not inferred from her style.
Which joy of hers merged into that of 15 August 1947 -- a narrated event. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2. (Stem is garbled: 'khushi samaa kar rah gayi thi'.)

Which of the father's traits are worth emulating -- an evaluative response to the father, which the policy places at LO-2. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: the text lists his traits but never ranks them as anukaraniya.
The effect of the father's finances on him -- the text spells it out. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a stated causal chain, not a judgement.
Why the father made her sit in the debates -- the stated motive. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content recall. (Same question as an MCQ earlier in this chapter, re-set as a 3-mark short answer.)

Which Jainendra novel she took to (Sunita) -- her reading as the lesson records it. Rejected C-H1.3 at competency level: unlike the pure authorship-attribution items, this asks what the text says she liked.
The doctor's name (Ambalal) -- a named character. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
The cause of the clash with her father (difference of ideas) -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a reported cause, not a reaction to his authoritarianism.
The mother's temperament (self-sacrificing) -- recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Metropolitan life is devoid of warmth -- the passage says so. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: a stated conclusion, not an appraisal of how she argues it.
The father's temperament (suspicious) -- recall. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Which movement she joined (the freedom struggle) -- a narrated life event. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
What the dictionary brought the father (fame and standing) -- stated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2.
Who inspired her to write (father and Hindi lecturer) -- named in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: it asks who, not how her style formed.
The real causes of the differences between her and her father -- the text supplies them. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: an abhivyakti answer built from narrated content.
Which people influenced her and in what way -- enumerated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content, not mantavya.

Why the kitchen is called a 'bhatiyarkhana' -- a loaded word whose connotation and the contempt it carries are the point, i.e. bhasha-shaili. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: the text never explains the word, the student must read its tone.
Why she and her father clashed in outlook -- the causes are narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the text answers it directly.
What aatmakatha is as a vidha -- the policy routes genre questions (aatmakatha / sansmaran / kahani) to LO-2. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: nothing about the lesson's content is being tested.
The clash with her father over her part in the freedom struggle, with examples -- all narrated. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the events are in the text, no judgement on his authority is asked for.

Sketch the freedom-movement scene from this aatmakathya and mark her role -- content drawn from the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: the word aatmakathya is only a pointer, the genre itself is not what is tested.
Sheela Agrawal's role in turning her from ordinary to extraordinary -- narrated in the text. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-2: content, not craft.

HOW the writer makes the value of neighbourhood culture felt -- her method of putting the point across, i.e. bhasha-shaili and mantavya. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: the companion items that ask what pados culture is take LO-1; this one asks how she conveys it.

Prove from the lesson that a teacher shapes a pupil's character -- this asks for the chapter's sandesh, the point the lekhika leaves the reader with. Rejected C-H1.3-LO-1: no single narrated fact answers it, the student must state what the piece is saying.
